language_wrapper: On an {height} by {width} chessboard whose opposite edges are identified to form a torus, a black/white coloring is called valid if exactly {k} squares are black and no two black squares are adjacent by a king move (i.e., horizontally, vertically, or diagonally), with adjacency understood cyclically across the edges. Determine the number of valid colorings.
hardness_rationale: The seed counts independent sets on an n×n grid graph (rook adjacency) and sums small n. Our family imposes king adjacency (including diagonals) and toroidal boundary conditions, and fixes the exact number of black squares. This transforms the problem into counting weighted independent sets on a cyclic transfer graph with a cycle closure constraint, requiring a transfer-matrix dynamic programming with compatibility across rows and a final wrap-around condition. The exact-k constraint adds a knapsack-like dimension to the DP. These elements eliminate simple guessing and substantially increase the combinatorial and algorithmic difficulty while preserving the core idea of forbidden adjacencies in grid colorings.
notes: Proof sketch: Model each row by a bitmask of length w with no adjacent 1s under cyclic adjacency; these are precisely the independent sets of the cycle C_w. Two consecutive rows m and n are compatible under king adjacency iff m∧n = 0 and m∧(n shifted left/right cyclically) = 0, which encodes the vertical and diagonal attack prohibitions, including wrap-around horizontally. Build a transfer directed graph whose vertices are valid row masks and edges correspond to compatibility. Counting colorings of an h-row torus is equivalent to counting closed walks of length h in this graph whose total weight (sum of 1s across rows) equals k. The DP initializes at a chosen first row mask m_0, advances h−1 steps accumulating the number of black squares, and enforces the cycle closure by requiring the last mask to be compatible with m_0. Summing over all choices of m_0 counts each toroidal coloring exactly once. Correctness follows from bijection between colorings and compatible sequences of row masks satisfying the closure condition. Complexity is bounded by O(h·|M|^2·k), where |M| is the number of independent sets on C_w (~Lucas number), which is tractable for widths up to 7. This approach generalizes the seed’s transfer idea to stronger adjacency, periodic boundaries, and fixed-size constraints.
source_question: The number of ways to color an \(n \times n\) chessboard with black and white such that no neighboring two blocks can be black simultaneously is \(x_n\). Find \(\sum_{n=2}^5 x_n\)．
